name: Git container config
description: Re-applies, on every container create, the user-scope git settings a devcontainer needs and cannot keep: LFS filters for the remote user, worktree.useRelativePaths, safe.directory, and an include.path to an identity file — read from one fixed mount point, /usr/local/share/devc-features/git-container-config/identity/gitconfig, if a consumer has bind-mounted one there. No path option: that mount point is the one thing a consumer decides is what to bind onto. ~/.gitconfig is container-local and wiped on every rebuild, while the repo's working tree and .git are host bind mounts, so anything git needs at user scope has to be re-applied on every create. Installs neither git nor git-lfs — it configures a git that is already there.

lfsFilters.description: Run `git lfs install --force --skip-repo` for the remote user when git-lfs is on PATH. Needed because a git-lfs Feature that installs at build time (as root) writes its filters to /root/.gitconfig, which the remote user never sees. No git-lfs on PATH warns and continues rather than failing create.

lfsSkipSmudge.description: Add --skip-smudge to the LFS install above, so a checkout does not materialize LFS objects — most work does not need them and checkouts stay fast. Run `git lfs pull` (all) or `git lfs checkout -- <path>` (targeted) when you do; the clean filter stays active either way, so materialized files still read as unmodified.

worktreeRelativePaths.description: Set worktree.useRelativePaths so `git worktree add` run inside the container writes relative links instead of container-absolute paths a host could never resolve — the host and container mount the same .git at different absolute paths.

safeDirectory.description: Passed to `git config --global --replace-all safe.directory`. The workspace bind mount can present a different owner than the container user, which git otherwise refuses to operate on. Empty disables this setting entirely; any other value is passed through as-is, so a consumer can scope it to one path instead of `*`.
